question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what initial probe orientation is being established, and what is the main purpose of starting the exam this way?
A. Oblique orientation aligned with an anatomic landmark to optimize the acoustic window and reduce shadowing from overlying structures
B. Transverse (short-axis) orientation to quickly identify midline anatomy and locate the target before detailed scanning
C. Long-axis orientation to obtain accurate measurements of the target structure rather than to establish a survey plane
D. Long-axis (sagittal) orientation to establish the initial survey plane
groundtruth: The operator places the transducer in the sagittal plane to establish the initial scanning plane for the exam.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, the image window appears suboptimal early on. What check/adjustment is being performed, and why?
A. Increasing overall gain to brighten the near and far field when the image appears uniformly undergained.
B. Checking whether a fluid-filled window is adequate to improve penetration and pelvic visualization
C. Increasing imaging depth to include the posterior pelvis and bring deeper structures into the field of view.
D. Repositioning and angling the probe to obtain a different suprapubic acoustic window when the initial view is limited.
groundtruth: The operator scans inferiorly to evaluate bladder volume, recognizing it is not full; despite the limited acoustic window, they attempt to visualize the vagina and cervix.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what probe movement strategy is being used, and what is the goal of that movement?
A. Sliding the probe (translation) along the skin to follow a structure longitudinally and map its extent.
B. Applying graded compression to displace bowel gas and improve visualization of deeper abdominal structures.
C. Repetitive fanning/rocking through the organ to obtain a complete overall survey
D. Rotating the probe 90° to obtain an orthogonal view and confirm anatomy in two planes.
groundtruth: The operator scans back and forth through the uterus to obtain an overall view of uterine structure.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what is the operator primarily trying to determine during the continued systematic sweep?
A. Whether fetal cardiac activity is present to confirm viability
B. Whether there are any adnexal masses or free pelvic fluid suggesting an ectopic pregnancy
C. Whether there is a single gestation with only one fetus present
D. Whether the crown–rump length can be measured to estimate gestational age
groundtruth: The operator continues sweeping through the uterus to establish that there is a single pregnancy with only one fetus.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what major probe re-orientation is performed, and what is its purpose?
A. Fanning/sweeping the probe through a small arc to interrogate the region in multiple slices and identify the optimal window.
B. Rocking (tilting) the probe to better center the structure in a long-axis view and maximize its apparent length.
C. Heel-toe angulation of the probe to steer the beam toward the target and improve endocardial border definition without changing axis.
D. Rotating the probe ~90° to switch into a short-axis (transverse) assessment
groundtruth: The operator rotates the transducer 90 degrees to transition from sagittal to transverse imaging.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, after finding the low starting landmark, what optimization movement is performed next and why?
A. A slow controlled slide upward to maintain orientation and avoid skipping key anatomy
B. A gentle heel-toe (rocking) maneuver to bring the target into the center of the beam and maximize sharpness.
C. A small clockwise rotation to align the probe with the long axis of the structure before continuing the sweep.
D. A brief fan (tilt) through the region to confirm the landmark in two planes before moving cranially.
groundtruth: After identifying the bladder low in the pelvis, the operator slowly slides superiorly to move the field of view upward from the bladder.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video segment, which exam step is being carried out, and what is the broader goal of the sequence?
A. Mid-sagittal longitudinal uterine sweep to center the gestational sac and obtain dating measurements such as CRL.
B. Focused adnexal interrogation with color Doppler to assess ovarian blood flow and exclude torsion or ectopic pregnancy.
C. Systematic transverse pelvic survey including lateral side evaluation to complete early pregnancy assessment
D. Targeted cervical and lower uterine segment scan to evaluate cervical canal integrity and look for signs of impending miscarriage.
groundtruth: In transverse imaging, the operator starts low to identify the bladder as a landmark, slides superiorly, angles to the right adnexa to see the right ovary/corpus luteum, and continues scanning superiorly through the pelvis to confirm only one baby.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what image optimization is performed to improve inspection of small internal details, and why?
A. Decreasing imaging depth to focus the field of view on the region of interest without magnifying it
B. Activating tissue harmonic imaging to reduce clutter and improve border definition instead of increasing apparent size
C. Zooming in to increase apparent size/resolution of the area of interest
D. Adjusting overall gain and time-gain compensation to improve brightness/contrast rather than detail size
groundtruth: The operator focuses on the contents of the gestational sac and zooms the image to optimize resolution for inspecting the sac contents.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what is the operator’s strategy for resolving uncertainty about viability, and what is the goal?
A. Optimize depth/gain and sweep through multiple planes to ensure the embryo is truly in view before deciding on viability.
B. Activate M-mode to obtain a heart rate tracing for documentation of viability.
C. Turn on color Doppler to look for intracardiac flow and distinguish true activity from artifact.
D. Watching for intrinsic rhythmic motion to confirm cardiac activity
groundtruth: The operator assesses the fetus for motion in order to visualize fetal cardiac activity.
